name: Hak5 Bash Bunny
description: An advanced SoC-based attack platform capable of simultaneously emulating a gigabit Ethernet adapter, mass storage, and a high-speed keyboard. It specializes in bypassing firewalls via rogue RNDIS networking and extracting credentials.
ioc_indicators: Sudden enumeration of a new RNDIS/Ethernet interface followed by anomalous SMB or HTTP traffic to a link-local IP (e.g., 172.16.64.1).
mitigation_actions: Network Rule: Disable auto-configuration of new RNDIS/Ethernet-over-USB network interfaces.
Hardware Rule: Block composite USB devices that enumerate both HID and Networking classes simultaneously.
Behavioral: Monitor for rapid sequential execution of PowerShell or CMD binaries.

name: Hak5 O.MG Cable
description: A highly covert malicious implant concealed within a standard USB charging cable. It establishes a hidden Wi-Fi access point (C2 channel) allowing remote attackers to trigger delayed keystroke payloads and exfiltrate data.
ioc_indicators: Presence of an Apple keyboard VID/PID (05ac:021e) when no physical Apple keyboard is attached. Abnormal power consumption for a passive charging cable.
mitigation_actions: Physical Security: Implement strict clean-desk policies and ban BYOD (Bring Your Own Device) cables.
Hardware Rule: Alert on generic Apple/Logitech VIDs that draw power exceeding standard HID limits.
Network/RF Rule: Monitor the physical environment for unauthorized rogue Wi-Fi APs (O.MG default SSIDs).

name: Hak5 Rubber Ducky
description: The quintessential keystroke injection tool. It emulates a generic USB keyboard to blindly inject pre-compiled payloads (DuckyScript) at speeds far exceeding human capabilities, executing code before the OS can mount defenses.
ioc_indicators: Keystroke event delta (time between key presses) consistently falling below 50ms with zero variance (robotic precision).
mitigation_actions: Behavioral: Enforce strict keystroke dynamic analysis (speed and variance checks).
OS Rule: Require active user interaction (e.g., Ctrl+Alt+Del) before executing auto-run prompts.
Endpoint Rule: Blacklist known default Ducky VIDs if observed outside expected peripheral lists.

name: Digispark (V-USB BadUSB)
description: A low-cost, Arduino-compatible development board utilizing software-based USB emulation (V-USB). Frequently weaponized by script kiddies for rapid deployment of reverse shells or ransomware downloaders.
ioc_indicators: Device enumeration logs showing 'Digispark' or the specific V-USB VID 16d0, coupled with short connection lifespans.
mitigation_actions: Hardware Rule: Immediately block VID 16d0:0753, as it is strictly a development board and has no legitimate enterprise use case.
Behavioral: Alert on devices that disconnect immediately after less than 10 seconds of connection time.

name: Teensy LC (Weaponized)
description: A versatile microcontroller capable of emulating keyboards, mice, and serial ports simultaneously. Often used in targeted physical penetration tests due to its larger memory capacity for complex, multi-stage payloads.
ioc_indicators: Multiple input interfaces (Mouse, Keyboard, Serial) registering simultaneously under the PJRC/Teensy VID (16c0).
mitigation_actions: Hardware Rule: Restrict devices presenting as generic HID from loading serial port (COM) drivers simultaneously.
Behavioral: Correlate simultaneous mouse movement and rapid keyboard typing originating from the same physical port.

name: Inverse Path USB Armory
description: A full-featured computer in a USB stick form factor. While designed for secure applications, it can be weaponized as a malicious network adapter to intercept local traffic, steal hashed credentials (Responder), or poison DNS caches.
ioc_indicators: Appearance of the Linux Foundation VID (1d6b) registering as a Communications and CDC Control network interface.
mitigation_actions: Network Rule: Deny network bridging or sharing from internal Wi-Fi/Ethernet to USB-based network adapters.
Protocol Rule: Deploy NTLM relay mitigations (SMB Signing) to render stolen hashes useless.
Endpoint Rule: Alert on any unexpected changes to the host's default gateway or DNS routing table post-USB insertion.
